<thought>Based on the mass (M+H⁺ = 141.115, neutral ≈ 140.1 Da) and the 13C NMR (carbonyl ~167 ppm, two sp² carbons ~144 and 130 ppm, plus several aliphatic carbons), a plausible formula is C₈H₁₂O₂ (DBE = 3). The ¹H NMR shows only singlet methyl signals (3 H, 6 H, 6 H), suggesting a structure with three types of methyl groups and no aromatic or olefinic protons, consistent with an α,β‑unsaturated ester bearing tert‑butyl‑like methyl groups. A reasonable candidate is **tert‑butyl acrylate**, SMILES: `CC(C)(C)OC(=O)C=C`. This matches the carbonyl, the C=C carbons, and provides three methyl environments (two equivalent methyls on the tert‑butyl, one methyl on the same carbon). I will validate this SMILES.</thought>
